t:
[Map missing]

Climate: Temperate, closest to Darkwater.

Affiliation: Neutral allod; before the undead curse it belonged to Kania.

Story:

We are met by the Kanian woman Vlasta Shukhova in a camp on the shore. She tells us that Catherina sent her to this allod to gather deathcap mushrooms, which she needs for a potion for speaking with the dead. According to her, they grow only here (actually they also grow in Jeer's Mansion). We agree to help her. Also in the camp is the aviak mercenary Daris. He complains that everything is bad: his sword broke, his comrades Amis, Atis and Potis died, a black raven flew past. He asks us to bring back the rings of his fallen comrades; he will carry them to his homeland. After we bring the deathcaps, Vlasta says that now we can overcome Fiercefang, who lives here; she makes a calming potion, and we are to use it when he goes berserk. In that state we would not defeat him. We find the first ring on Fiercefang. We find the second ring on a bunch of zombie warriors by a hut near the bridge (there is a chest of gold in it). We make our way into the settlement with the church, clearing out hordes of undead, and there we kill the Cursed Banshee Tear, and on her we pick up the last, third ring. In one of the huts is the Kanian necromancer Bolegost Mrakov. After the victory over him we pick up his diary. Judging by the entries, Bolegost, trying to save the island from a demon attack, decided to resort to an army of undead, made an elixir from deathcaps, but miscalculated the dose, went mad, and believed that the demons were still invading. It's a good thing we put an end to his madness. And we will send the diary to Umoir. We give it to Vlasta. "I'll pass this document on to the Umoir archive. If you ask me, this Bolegost is a hero! Just a poor unfortunate one."

Bosses: Fiercefang, Tear, Bolegost Mrakov.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Addendum: Over time it was reworked into Wolf Isle.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Temperate, closest to Darkwater.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, a former Kanian settlement, now inhabited by the undead.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

The island of Silent Hills always served me as proof that in the future we and the Kanians will be able to live in peace. I didn't visit it often, but when I did, I talked without fear to simple Kanians tending their modest farms, and stocked up on their freshly baked, extraordinarily tasty bread. They didn't care a whit about the feud between Tensess and Nezeb, about the war between the League and the Empire... Now ghosts are the masters there. They go about their business as before: they fish, hunt, grind flour. And they were not at all glad to see either me or my crew. We barely got away. I am at a loss! What evil has appeared in Silent Hills? Who cursed the poor souls? If you have the courage to take up the challenge of this mystery, follow my advice. Look for the cause of Silent Hills' misfortunes in the dark forest! The peasants always gave that place a wide berth. Perhaps one of them broke the age-old order and woke the evil slumbering there. Obstacles will surely stand in your way, and you'll have to overcome them to reach the source of the evil. Remember that you won't manage to cleanse the island without fighting its ghostly inhabitants. That is the pain you'll have to go through. Know that you bring them not death, but release from the Darkness.

Bosses: Tsar Pike, Elder Miller, the Bane of Silent Hills.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by undead.

Story:

We arrive on the island, and a family of Seekers asks us for help. Lara, Indie and Nathan need to get into the tower for artifacts; to do so, several shards have to be collected and the sentry blocking the passage defeated. First we head into the thicket, where its inhabitants greet us aggressively; once we have cleared the thicket we find Sylvan, who complains that he will have to drive us off the allod himself. We defeat him, and Indie takes the shard. Next we make our way through the swamp, killing everyone who crosses our path, and reach the Silent Guard, who will not let us go further. Once they are defeated, Lara finds one more shard. We make our way through the ruins, again killing enemies. We find a passage, but it is guarded by the Sentry; we activate it and defeat it. After that the way into the Tower opens, and together with the Seeker family we defeat Veliyar. The gibberlings thank us for our help.

Bosses: Sylvan, Kodo the Silent and Nigan the Silent, Sentry, Veliyar.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Temperate. Closest to Avilon.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by sirens.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler).

Have you ever heard the legends about the beautiful singing of sirens that lures the ships of hapless sailors onto the reefs? Well — those aren't legends, but harsh reality. On one of the distant islands an elven tribe has settled — I can't bring myself to call that rabble anything else. Astronauts report that songs and music drift from Sirens' Rock containing some evil magic that makes the crew steer the ship straight to its doom. Resisting the magic is hard, but possible, if there is a talented specialist on board. Though some deaf bruiser will do just as well. The amount of shipwreck debris around the island speaks for itself. It's hard even to imagine how many honest sailors have fallen victim to those bloodthirsty creatures! And where are they now, what have those creatures done with them? Eaten them? I have, by the way, reports of undead sighted on the Rock... I advise you to avoid this island at any cost. Although, by rights, of course, it's long past time to send a squad of adepts there to mow that scum down from a safe distance.

Bosses: Levoxia, Cock Pit, Ligea, Molpa and the Demon of Madness.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Tundra, closest to Coldberg.

Affiliation: Imperial allod, a holiday camp.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

I know, I know about that resort. The apotheosis of universal stupidity, not a resort. You know how scholars love to show off their technology and play at being conquerors of nature. Well, they took it into their heads to create a resort not just anywhere, but in the middle of the eternal ice. They found a suitable islet, freezing cold — terrible! They raised a dome there and built a whole little town under it. Imagine: all around a blizzard whistles, and inside the birds sing and the grass grows green... Bliss, in a word. Only our clever folk didn't take into account that a tribe of wild orcs lives in the caves there. They fed mainly on mountain goats and cave mushrooms. And when the engineers were building the dome, they sealed an underground stream in concrete. And the orcs were left with nothing at all to eat: the goats died off, the mushrooms withered. So they went to war with the resort's guards. And the guards there are first-rate, veterans to a man. No doubt they thought the big shots would be coming skiing. They made a great secret of it all — one step outside the perimeter and they shoot without warning. I wanted to unload some field rations from my hold for them, and they opened fire on me. Started blasting at an Imperial ship without a word! I barely got away. What secrets could they have there...

Bosses: Shakhrai-Gor, Pavel Syrin, Vyacheslav Lapochkin, Alexander Burdakin.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Temperate, closest to the Al Rihat Ruins.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by renegade Kanian sorcerers.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler).

The Workshop? Why yes, I've heard of it... It's a strange place, I tell you. And an evil one.

They say that sorcerers of every stripe used to gather there to practice their arts in peace and quiet. They practiced until they began experimenting on Sparks — capturing them by force and moving them into other bodies. A regular branch of Tep's Pyramid. Naturally, everyone turned against the sorcerers at once — both the League and the Empire. Only the sorcerers had no wish to abandon their experiments, and threw everyone who disagreed with them into the Astral. Ever since, sheer devilry has been going on on that island. Those who have flown past say the sorcerers started felling the forest and building wooden soldiers and golems. And — just think of it! — that whole wooden army has come to life and seems to be preparing to attack our allods. That's where experiments with Sparks lead.

Bosses: Rustle, Burian Jagger and Gurrian Jagger, Yarosvat Zoriev, Porfiry Polenov.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Temperate, closest to Darkwater.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, a termite nest.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

What do astronauts fear? Everyone knows: demons and anomalies. But recently another plague has appeared. One after another, battered ships came into port, and their crews told of swarms of termites flying through the Astral as if across a green lawn. Once such a swarm flew all the way to Nezebgrad itself! They were shot down, of course, while still on approach, but the question remained: how do these insects scurry about in a hostile medium that dissolves everything, living and non-living? I heard that a private merchant managed to catch a few specimens and dissect them. In the insects' abdomens he found traces of meteorite dust — that is what protected them! Now the Free Traders promise a tidy sum to anyone who finds the nest of these creatures. Many rushed off in search of it... Only, I fear, it is their own death they are searching for. Can you imagine how huge the termite mound must be? If I knew where it was — be there meteorite, gold or gems — I would give it a wide berth!

Bosses: Ground Beetle, Murava, Itch, Chrysalis.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

[Map missing]

Climate: Taiga, closest to Siveria.

Affiliation: League allod, a Gibberling settlement.

Story:

In the game the island had no NPCs. We arrive on the island at a makeshift pier, next to which is a mini-fort with astral cannons. Further on we see burning huts, and also books gathered in a pile and set on fire. The allod itself is a mountain, and the higher we climb along the paths, the more corpses of Gibberlings and Kanians we meet. At the very top stands the main hut; on the other side of the allod the houses are empty but not burned.

Bosses: no information.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

t:
Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by Tep's cultists.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Ah, so the rumours about that island have reached you too? A mysterious place. An ancient June forge, now seized by Tep's cultists. What goes on there, nobody knows. I heard of a group of desperate travellers who dared to penetrate the belly of the ancient volcano where the forge is located. Only one managed to come back. According to him, Tep's cultists are trying to take control of the ancient June mechanisms, to make them their loyal servants. If they succeed… The genius of the June plus the madness of Tep... Oh dear, oh dear... Be extremely careful if you dare to challenge this explosive mixture.

Bosses: Tep's Punisher, Tep's Rider, Dark Mistress, Shadow Devourer.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Addendum: Over time reworked into an Island of the Astral Dominion.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
[Map missing]

Climate: Temperate, closest to Eljune.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, a smugglers' lair.

Story:

We land near a Free Traders' camp. We are met by the Gibberlings of the Earthy Family. They say they are waiting for their mercenaries, who are supposed to kill the smugglers. They complain about them: they knock down prices and don't pay duties. This allod should be destroyed altogether, so that they don't gather here anymore. The allod is held together by meteorite iron, which we will have to steal. The next to ask us for help is Marat Vykhin. According to him, the ship with the mercenaries has been missing for a very long time, and they (the Free Traders) could be discovered and killed at any moment. He asks us to kill their chief, Kolotun the Forester, and then the rest will start fighting for power. The third, Khvoshch the Rowdy, says that they are out of money: he went into the forest to relieve himself and was spotted by the local Forestfolk. Now they are blackmailing the orc, saying that as long as he brings them a precious stone a day, they won't hand the traders over to the smugglers. In short, he asks us to deal with the Forestfolk and their chief, Barefoot. After clearing out the Forestfolk and the Camp, and also gathering the meteorite iron, we are thanked for our help. Khvoshch says that now the 10 sapphires they swindled out of him somehow have to be quietly slipped back to Marat, and asks us not to spread word of what happened.

Bosses: Forestfolk Chief Barefoot, Kolotun the Forester.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
[Map missing]

Climate: Desert, closest to the Dead Sea.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, an old Imperial base settled by orcs and goblins.

Story:

No sooner have we stepped off the ship than Tep's cultists attack us. After defeating them, we free a goblin named Sypun. He fearfully asks whether we are going to beat him. Once he is sure he is safe, he tells us about the situation on the allod. The goblin Zanud (the Supreme Shaman) declared these lands an independent goblin republic. They separated from the orcs, but then the water ran out. Since the water remained with the orcs, the goblins decided to attack them, but got a thrashing. Then "suicide men" appeared on the allod — that is what Zanud called Tep's cultists — and drove the orcs out. Now both the orcs and the goblins are on the verge of death because they have no water. The goblin sends us to their village to talk to Zanud. In short, Zanud didn't add many details; he only specified that the Cultists had seized the lake, the so-called Puddle, and won't let anyone near it; they are doing something there. We are asked to drive them out of there and to kill their chief — he sits in the former orc camp. The goblins will have water, and the orcs will fall before their might and beg the goblins to share the water. After the victory over the Shepherd, we find the orc woman Koryaga in a cage. She says that helping the foolish goblins is a bad idea: the Real locals are the Orcs; they stayed here to live after the night of astral portals, in the old Imperial camp. Their shaman Lysukha sent her to scout, but Koryaga was captured and so never found out what the cultists are looking for here. She asks us to intercept the punitive squad that has headed for the orcs and to kill their chief punisher. After the victory over the Commander, Lysukha thanks us for the rescue and says that before the orcs were driven out, the Commander tried to win them over to his side, saying they would restore Tep's power; she suggests we find and destroy the sources of Tep's power. In the old Zem ruins we find a mechanism; after activating it, the Shard of Tep appears, and we destroy it. After its destruction an orc woman crawls out of the sand and says that she hid and saw us destroy that thing; she thanks us, says she will tell Lysukha everything, and that we will be honored.

Bosses: Shepherd, Servant of Tep; Commander, Cultist of Tep; Shard of Tep.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Temperate, closest to Darkwater.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, forest fauna and an expedition camp.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler).

Just a second, let me look in my notes. Hmm... Aha, here it is! An entry about a new island being added to the astral sailing directions, on which old June ruins were discovered. Right, right... In short, I know almost nothing about this island. It doesn't even have a name! According to our intelligence, a Kanian scout ship discovered, in the depths of the Astral, an island on which June ruins from the time of the rise of June civilization had survived. Since the ruins are of enormous scientific value, the League hastily sent a ship to the island with an archaeological expedition led by a certain Nastasya Zhmurova. The expedition reached the island and began excavating, after which contact with them was lost. The last message said that the scholars had almost broken through the passage to the central crypt of the June tomb. They also complained about kobolds that had turned up from who knows where. At present nothing is known of the expedition's fate. If you want my opinion — the scholars dug up what should not have been dug up. The thirst for knowledge, like the thirst for gain, leads to no good.

Bosses: Mamba, Capa, Twisthorn, Nastasya Zhmurova.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Desert, closest to the Catacombs.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, a haven of the Wormfaces.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Looking for treasure, are you? Heh-heh... There's no treasure there! Only sand, the blazing sun, heat and scorpions nesting among the ruins. As a Historian I know told me, there was once a huge observatory there, in which June priests studied the movement of the sun and stars and compiled solar and lunar calendars and the most detailed horoscopes. And now all that is left of the temple-observatory is ruins half-buried in sand. Not so long ago the Wormfaces returned to the Tlalkoa Ruins. They cleared out some of the halls, repaired the old battle golems and jealously guard the ruins against any intrusion. Their leader, who I gather is called Mirage, desperately needs something in those ruins, and he will not hesitate to kill anyone who enters beneath the vaults of the old temple. Luckily I got away in time, or else my bones too would be drying in the hot desert sun now...

Bosses: Isides, Rattler, Horatrix, Mirage.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Temperate, closest to Dane.

Affiliation: League allod, inhabited by Kanians and elves.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

An interesting little place. I haven't been there for a long while... And no wish to go, to be honest. Just a few years ago Triplefield was a lively trading town. What didn't they sell at the local market — elven gems, peasant bast shoes, Kanian armor... And then some disaster befell them: the dead rose and devoured the whole town, and few survived. The survivors brought down the only bridge leading to the town and settled in a small village some way off from the cursed ruins. Fortunately, the elves, whose enclave was nearby, were not affected by the curse that fell upon the town, and helped the surviving people set up at least some kind of peaceful life. But Triplefield will never see its former glory — now it's just a backwater hole. Still, I've heard that the League Church recently sent a squad of inquisitors there, and now I'm wondering — what could churchmen have lost in that Light-forsaken place?

Bosses: Alister de Doucer, Mstislav Ferocious, Milava Troepolskaya, Alex Gordev.

Type: Medium island. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Temperate, closest to Lightwood.

Affiliation: League allod, a Kanian settlement seized by cultists.

Story:
Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

You know about that one too? Hm... Strictly speaking, it isn't an island at all. It's a giant turtle that swims eternally through the astral. It's so enormous that a whole village lives on its back! Or rather, lived... Here's the thing... Two noblemen, the Zalesky brothers, mighty sorcerers, decided that the present authorities didn't suit them. They resolved to raise a revolt — for selfish reasons, of course. But Aidenus quickly learned of the treachery. The brothers gathered their retinue, loaded onto a ship and dashed off wherever their eyes led them. And their eyes spotted Turtle Island. They moored at the shore; the peasants saw the lordly ship and greeted the renegades with bread and salt, and in return the renegades put them to a cruel death! Only a few hunters managed to flee and hide in the astral. They were picked up by a Kanian ship belonging to my friend, Afanasy Nikitov. And he told me this story. As I understand it, the brothers are now trying to bend the flying turtle to their will. Can you imagine what will happen if they succeed? If someone sent those brothers to their graves, I'd have nothing but thanks for that hero!

Bosses: Tikhon Yezhov, Hardshell, Gostemil Zalesky, Velerad Zalesky.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Tropical, closest to the Jungles of Mboa-Mboa.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by aviaks.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

A real pearl of the Astral! An Imperial resort would look perfect in such a place. But, alas, we will have to give up those plans — hostile aborigines now live on the island. Originally only one tribe of aviaks lived in the lagoon. At one time we managed to develop minimal trade relations with them. Pure barter — their hides and precious stones in exchange for our weapons. Unheard-of generosity on our part, by the way! Everyone knows there are no weapons in the world better than ours. But a little later certain pirates, whose names we will never learn now, attacked the lagoon, hoping to easily steal all our goods. The aviaks repelled the attack and in revenge plundered the pirates' ship. There, apparently, they found unhatched eggs and took them under their care. Unfortunately, they were lizard eggs. As soon as they hatched, the whole brood ran away from the aviaks to the other end of the island. Soon a second tribe of aborigines appeared in the lagoon. And so one stunt by idiots who had got their hands on the Astral dealt the Empire a blow, a weak one, but a blow nonetheless. The aviaks of Tusky Lagoon now regard the "wingless" with utter contempt. If you fly past, expect no hospitality.

Bosses: Rattle, Ssera-Hay, Cau the Stormbringer, Tsol the Bloodstained Feather.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Temperate; the climate on the shard is varied.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, the dwelling place of the months and the seasons of the year.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

The seasons... Long, long ago, when Sarnaut had not yet broken apart, these words meant more than a change of dates in the calendar. Nowadays, as they say, "spring is gone and summer's here, thanks to Yasker, never fear" — but back then the seasons changed on their own. Summer was followed by autumn, autumn by winter, then came spring and summer again. And so they went, one after another: one month decorously succeeding the other, neither lagging behind nor running ahead. But the Kanians have an old, old tale about a little girl who was lucky enough to see all twelve months at once! As if somewhere in the world there were a little grove where all twelve brother-months gathered once a year to discuss their year's doings. That's all old wives' tales, of course. Only a friend told me he had seen a strange islet in the far Astral. Like a glass ball, and inside it a grove with twelve fine young fellows. While they were flying past, the snow in the ball melted, grass peeped out, everything turned green and blossomed — and then in an instant turned yellow, withered, and the ground was dusted with snow again. They were just about to go closer, when — snap! — the island vanished as if it had never been. What do you think: maybe the tale told the truth? Maybe the brother-months are still alive, and that very grove is still intact?

Bosses: Winter, Spring the Fair, Autumn the Woeful, Bright Summer.

Type: Medium island. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Tropical, closest to the Pearl Ring.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by underwater dwellers.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

The Underwater Kingdom? To this day no one knows whether it really exists. I'm not in the habit of lying, so I'll tell you what I know myself. I heard this story from a Kanian merchant. His name was Sachkov, or maybe Sadkov. He was a rich merchant, he was friends with the Free Traders, and they say he even had his sights on becoming an Oligarch! He carried goods back and forth across the whole Astral and spent all his life on the road. His wife, clever and beautiful, saw her husband once every six months at best, but didn't complain. And one day Sadkov's ship happened to stray from the caravan route. He saw a small islet — not even an islet, just a scrap of land with a well and an abandoned hut. And the crew was just running out of water. They put in to shore, and Sadkov went to the well for a drink. No sooner had he bent over than a cold hand shot out of the well and grabbed him by the beard! And a muffled voice from under the water said: "Promise to give me what you have but do not know of, or else I'll drown you." Sadkov took fright and foolishly promised to give what he did not know of. If you don't know of it, you won't miss it! The water spirit let him go, and when the merchant got home he began tearing his hair out. His wife met him right on the doorstep with a little baby. The merchant was seized with horror — he had promised his own child to the vile water spirit! But it's not for nothing that merchants are taught to count first and write only afterwards. Sadkov remembered that he had last been home more than a year ago, and the baby wasn't even a month old! His dearest spouse's debit and credit didn't tally — the child turned out to be someone else's. Sadkov threw his wayward wife and the child out of the house to go wherever they pleased, and gave his clerk, who had stayed behind to mind the business, a proper beating — the child looked a great deal like the clerk. And from then on the merchant drank himself into a stupor and drank away his whole fortune down to the last copper. And when the water spirit came for his due at the appointed time, the merchant advised him to look for his pledge himself, and paid out the interest on the loan in kicks and cuffs. That's the sad tale. If you see a small islet with a well in the Astral — don't be lazy, throw a keg of explosives down the well, so that the wretched water spirit who drives honest people into poverty won't find life a bed of roses!

Bosses: Bereginya, Goldfeather Fish, Blackmarin, Sea King.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

m.credit: Allods atlas and community lore material compiled by Makar Terentiev (DarkyAndSparky), https://github.com/DarkyAndSparky/atlas-ao

t:
Climate: Tundra, closest to Coldberg.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, the grave of a June hunter.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Have you ever heard of the island of Vortex? A lump of ice-covered land floating in the Astral. The grave of a Great Dragon that died back in the time of the June. For many thousands of years its ghost has guarded its grave. Meanwhile the depths of this island hold considerable reserves of meteorite iron. The Empire has a vital interest in capturing it. Perhaps you will manage to do it? Then remember this. To reach the ghost you will have to fight ice elementals, wild yetis living in a cave, and harpies guarding the passage to the Great Dragon's grave. Only once you are next to it will you be able to see the ghost and defeat it. Will you take it on?

Bosses: Yeti Tribal Chief, Valeryanych, Ghost of the Great Dragon.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island. Confrontation island.

Addendum: Based on the Grave Island. Over time reworked into an Island of the Astral Dominion.
f: Based on Grave Isle. Later reworked into an Astral Dominion island.

t:
Climate: Tundra, closest to Coldberg.

Affiliation: Imperial allod, a secret laboratory.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

Yes, I have heard of such a town. White 17 is a classified military settlement hidden somewhere deep in the Astral. And, as far as I know, there is something there to hide. You see, in White 17 Imperial scientists were engaged in extremely dangerous research. I don't know for sure, but rumour has it that Nomarkh Ebol, the lead researcher, maintained a very close relationship with Yasskul Setnakhte. Well, I have already told you about Yasskul Setnakhte and the incident at Lab Nine. And recently contact with White 17 was lost. Completely. Not a letter, not a messenger, not a single word... I fear some misfortune may have struck there, like the one that befell General Plague and his subordinates. So if in your wanderings you come across a snow-covered island guarded by Imperial soldiers, better turn back at once. But if you do risk landing there and get into trouble, look for Valentin Shtammin, an acquaintance of mine. He is listed there as chief mechanic, I believe. Oh, my heart tells me something is wrong with this White 17...

Bosses: Distemper, Venomisk, Crunch, Nomarkh Ebol.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

t:
Climate: Temperate, closest to Gipat.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by goblins.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

I happened to go there as part of a missionary and educational mission. You see, a tribe of utterly wild goblins lives on the White Mountain. The poor wretches do not even know who the Great Nezeb is! A thoroughly benighted people, and an aggressive one too! They wanted to sacrifice our missionaries to some scaly creature which the local goblins consider — just imagine — a god! Sacrilege, pure and simple!

When the missionaries and I left the island, a punitive detachment of the Committee arrived there to instil in the filthy pagans the fundamentals of the true faith, mutual respect and reverence for the Trinity Church. What happened on the island I do not know, but I do know that the Committee men came back from the island thoroughly battered and as furious as a thousand dragons, after which the coordinates of the island and the records of the two expeditions the Empire had made to the White Mountain were classified. But from rumours and gossip I heard of some idol worshipped by the shaggy wild runts, which supposedly gave its servants the strength to cope with seasoned Imperial fighters. If your path leads to the White Mountain, remember: fanatics do not heed the voice of reason. Brute force is the only thing they understand well!

Bosses: Mosol, Potbelly, Kazhetan, I'do-ol.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

t:
Climate: Temperate, closest to Darkwater.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, formerly Kanian.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

In my wanderings I always give Wolf Isle a wide berth. An ancient legend tied to this deadly place tells of a Kanian village that became a feeding ground for a werewolf. They say that long, long ago a Kanian druid named Vseslav the Charming grew so close to the wolves living on the island that he learned to change into wolf shape. He became the leader of the pack, and his neighbours its first victims. In time nobody was left there but wolves and werewolves. Hapless travellers who dare to land on the island become a welcome treat for its inhabitants. If you long to perform a heroic deed, Wolf Isle is quite a fitting place. But here is my advice: think a hundred times before you challenge the pack!

Bosses: Chernobog, the Bane of Wolf Isle, Vseslav the Charming.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Addendum: Based on the Umoir Shard.

t:
Climate: Tropical, closest to Asee-Teph.

Affiliation: Neutral allod, inhabited by the Waterfolk Tribe.

Story:

The allod was part of the Holy Land, like the Isle of the Dead; it broke off for unknown reasons. After landing and walking a little way, we come to a village of neutral Waterfolk. Rogoz (the chief of the neutral Waterfolk) speaks with us; he says that in the other settlements on this allod they still believe that the Whale-Fish saved the allod during the great splash, and they believed it too, until their prophet Leafy fell asleep at the altar in the center of the allod. He began to see visions and to enlighten us Waterfolk; he managed to tell… Our chief Bagor did not believe him and wants to sacrifice him. We agree to help him. We free Leafy. He says that he saw us in his visions, and also: "I dreamed a lot of things. I understood almost nothing. I dreamed of some dreadful creature with a big beard, chained to the sky. I dreamed of some monsters with tentacles on their faces... Oh, it's so complicated" (it is obvious to us that this is about Sarn). He also asks us to kill Bagor, who is preparing the place for the sacrifice. After our victory over Bagor, Leafy says that in another dream we defeat the Whale-Fish. And in yet another dream he becomes the leader on this boat-island. True, he refuses the power, but he still asks us to kill the Fish. After the victory Leafy says: "Now the lake turtles will gnaw the Whale-Fish's bones clean! It won't devour my people anymore!"

Bosses: Bagor, chief of the Waterfolk; Rybko the Whale-Fish.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Addendum: Over time it was reworked into the Shard of Power.

t:
Climate: Temperate, closest to Lightwood.

Affiliation: League allod, a Kanian colony.

Story:

We are met by serfs. They tell us that everything is fine on their island and that the allod is run by the lady Verona de Doucer. But in a whisper they ask us to go to the north of the allod and question the fugitives, for in truth they are oppressed here. At the astral shipyard we are met by Borodai Zalesky, a man of standing on the allod, who advises us to be sure to go to the lady. Verona tells us that she was invited here by Gordei Zalesky, but he died in her arms for unknown reasons, and his nephew asked her to stay and help run the allod. Gordei had invited other races to the allod — Gibberlings, orcs and so on — so that they would help the allod develop, but after his death they began to stir up unrest. We reach the fugitives' camp; there the Gibberlings tell the whole truth: the lady has set up a dictatorship, keeps everyone as slaves, they work themselves to the bone, and they are left only enough provisions to survive, but no more. The lady's troops had been spying on us; they attacked us, but we dealt with them. The Gibberling tells us the plan: he will raise the people against the remaining soldiers, and we are required to kill the lady, and the island will become free. As we approach the lady, we run into the voivode Zaruba Zalesky, and he has to be killed. A dialogue with Verona takes place, in which she says we are idiots and that she is the one holding the allod together, sends us to kill the chief conspirator, Otrad Zalesky, and goes off herself to calm the people.

After thinking over what had happened, the Gibberling shared his theory: the allod somehow held together even without the lady, so apparently Otrad was the one holding it, and he was most likely stupefied because of the golems the lady had brought with her. We stand at a crossroads: either we help return the allod to Otrad — switching off the golems, restoring his reason and killing Verona — or we kill Otrad and leave the island, for Verona no longer wants to see us on it.

Bosses: Zaruba Zalesky, Otrad Zalesky or Verona de Doucer.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

Addendum: Over time the story was changed somewhat.

t: I've been to this island. Bliss: green forests, singing streams... A settlement stands there — bigger than a village, smaller than a town. Red walls, a church with a bell tower, prosperous and friendly people. In a word, it's pleasant to visit and you can trade at a profit. They say, though, that some bandits have recently started threatening them. Well, they're not poor folk — they have enough gold to hire mercenaries for help. Or maybe you'll help them, show some heroism?

Climate: Temperate, closest to Lightwood.

Affiliation: League allod, inhabited by Kanians.

Story:

Astral island:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

I have been on that island. Bliss: green forests, singing streams... There stands a posad — bigger than a village, smaller than a town. Red walls, a church with a bell tower, prosperous and friendly people. In a word, it is pleasant to visit and profitable to trade there. True, they say some bandits have recently started threatening them. Well, they are not poor folk — they have enough gold to hire mercenaries. Or perhaps you will help them, show some heroism? We clear the allod, kill the bandits, and at the end the warlock too.

Story allod:

Catherina sent the Heroes to this island to obtain a real Firebird. The heroes set off. But an adventure awaited them as if they had truly stepped into a fairy tale. For first they clashed with dashing bandits who were robbing the villagers. They dealt with them and rescued the headman, who told them that the local druid, Nikodim Farouche, had the bird. And for his rescue the headman gave them a horse which could be traded for the bird. But on the way a werewolf attacked the heroes and devoured the horse; defeated, however, it promised to enter their service. Nikodim, of course, refused to simply hand over the bird and demanded another such horse, one that belonged to the local sorcerer — Mira Hooves. So the heroes went to Mira Hooves. For the horse he demanded that they perform three services for him. At first he asked them to do all sorts of nonsense, and then he gave them a hard task — the warlock Newsor Rotheart, he said, had abducted a maiden whom Mira Hooves wanted to take as his bride.

The heroes had to go and fight the warlock. Though he commanded the dead, he was nevertheless defeated and fled in disgrace. They returned to Mira Hooves with the rescued maiden, Milava Clairante. But he had already forgotten the bargain — so they had to calm him down too. Taking the horse, they went to Nikodim, but he too wanted Milava for himself. So he also had to be given a punch on the nose. And when they finally came to the pier with the bird, the two Gubarevsky brothers were waiting there, wanting to take the Firebird for themselves and bring it to Catherina themselves. They had to be dealt with as well.

Bosses:

Astral island: Mikhailo Potapych, Penny Pincher, Mira Hooves, Newsor Rotheart.

Story island: Newsor Rotheart, Nikodim Farouche, the Gubarevsky brothers.

Type: Medium island. Dungeon. Astral island. Umoir Archipelago. Story allod.

t:
Climate: Tropical, closest to …

Affiliation: Imperial allod, the site of a laboratory.

Story:

Fedor Stablemanov (Astral Traveler):

And why are you suddenly interested in Zone 51? You are not even supposed to know the name "Zone 51". It is classified information, I'll have you know! But I think that you, as a direct participant in the events at Laboratory 13, have the right to hear the truth about this secret military base of the Empire in the distant Astral. Listen carefully, and mind you don't let it slip! Zone 51 is a military laboratory in which, after the incident at Laboratory 13, experiments continued on the study of psychic influence on the mass consciousness. Nomarkh Sadaffee, the head of the project, decided to combine psionic influence with physical modification of the body. In his opinion, the imperfect human organism is not able to fully manipulate even its own consciousness, let alone influence others. And so he decided to combine the prosthetic technologies of the Arisen with psionic abilities. The combat mechanisms that resulted, controlled by the power of thought, could have become the ideal army — tireless, needing no resources, incapable of betrayal... But it was Nomarkh Sadaffee himself who became the traitor! According to the latest information, he managed to destroy or subjugate the entire guard of Zone 51. Contact with the military base was lost, and now nobody knows what is going on there. So if you see a pretty tropical islet in the Astral, where gloomy metal hangars peer out among the green jungle, know this — landing on that island may be the biggest mistake of your life... And quite possibly the last!

Bosses: Scar, Kiddo, Crash, Nomarkh Sadaffee.

Type: Small allod. Dungeon. Astral island.

t:
The land of Gipat, where your journey begins, resembles the temperate midlands in summer in its relief and vegetation. Beware of the apparent idyll and look around carefully; remember that Gipat's hostile and treacherous inhabitants are unpredictable! Trolls and goblins, bats, wolves, boars, hares and deer lie in wait for you. There are harpies too, in all their three-dimensional splendour. They are fabulously beautiful, but you must already know their foul temper well. More than once you will have to descend into natural caves, man-made mines and dungeons. Some of the dwellers of those worlds, who have never seen the sun or living people, will stay in your memory for a long time — if you manage to make it back to the surface, of course…

This island belongs to the group of orc islands. Its main population is orcs and goblins. The only village where people live is very small and constantly under threat of destruction. There is also a bandit camp whose members somehow manage to get along with the monsters. There is practically no metal here; people use bone and stone weapons and leather armour. Ruins of an unknown ancient civilization are found all over the island. It is small, and it belongs to none of the states because it is hard to reach and swarms with hostile monsters.

The Kanian Empire had plans to annex this land and had even built a fortress, but after the Cataclysm that split the world apart, the fortress and its garrison were left to fend for themselves. A handful of descendants of that garrison still live on Gipat, constantly fighting the goblins for the right to live.
